question: Two train lines intersect each other at a junction at an acute angle $\theta$. A train is passing along one of the two lines. When the front of the train is at the junction, the train subtends an angle $\alpha$ at a station on the other line. It subtends an angle $\beta\;(\beta<\alpha)$ at the same station, when its rear is at the junction. Show that $$\tan\theta=\frac{2\sin\alpha\sin\beta}{\sin(\alpha-\beta)}.$$

source.title: Test of Mathematics at the 10 + 2 Level
